customManagers.description: Bump the DEFAULTS block of the dependency ledger (deps.json). The recursive first matchString scopes extraction to defaults only — the overrides block (per-version / per-platform holds) is deliberately outside the region, so Renovate never touches a pinned hold. Only tag-pinned entries with a datasource are matched; commit pins (x264, amf) and tarball deps (gmp, libmp3lame) are hand-managed.

Track FFmpeg point releases in versions.txt — one line per maintained major.minor series (e.g. 8.1.2). Each line is a full x.y.z version; FFmpeg's upstream tags are n<version> (stripped via extractVersion). Only whole-line versions match, so comment text like the '8.1.2.0' example is ignored.

packageRules.description: Group all ledger dependency bumps under a clear prefix so CI (build + docs-matrix) validates each PR against every FFmpeg line before merge.

Keep review load low: batch routine (non-major) dependency bumps into ONE grouped PR per run instead of one PR per dep — so a quiet-to-busy week is a single PR + a single CI run to review and merge. MAJOR bumps are deliberately left ungrouped so each gets its own PR and individual scrutiny (they're the risky ones, e.g. an API-breaking codec major like x265 3->4). To go back to a PR per dep, delete this rule.

Vulkan-Headers/Loader + SPIRV-Headers ship in lockstep on vulkan-sdk-* release tags (the ledger pins the same SDK version across all three). Each repo ALSO carries a parallel v1.4.x tag scheme; restrict Renovate to the vulkan-sdk-* versioning so it can't cross namespaces or desync the trio (which it otherwise would — it proposed v1.4.360 for Loader+SPIRV but not Headers).

Constrain each FFmpeg line to its own major.minor series so Renovate only offers point releases (8.1.x, 9.0.x) and never a cross-series jump (8.1.x -> 9.x). One rule per maintained series; matchCurrentVersion scopes the rule to the line at that series, allowedVersions filters candidates to that series. Adding a new maintained series (check-updates.yml opens that as its own PR) means adding a matching rule here.
